<section class="article-section">

    <div class="articles-list">
      <div class="article-category">
        <h2>Pendulum Models</h2>
        <p style="margin-bottom: 2rem; font-size: 1.1rem; line-height: 1.8; color: var(--text-dark);">
          Pendulum-based models and simulations that serve as simplified analogs for understanding 
          golf swing dynamics. These models provide insights into control-affine systems, drift-input 
          decomposition, and the fundamental physics of underactuated multibody systems.
        </p>
      </div>

      <div class="article-category">
        <h2>Model Types</h2>
        <div class="article-card">
          <h3>Single Pendulum Models</h3>
          <p>Simple pendulum models with various actuation schemes, including torque at the pivot 
          and control inputs along the pendulum length. These models illustrate basic concepts in 
          control-affine systems and drift dynamics.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-card">
          <h3>Double Pendulum Models</h3>
          <p>Double pendulum (two-link) models that more closely approximate the complexity of 
          golf swing dynamics. Includes models with different actuation configurations and analysis 
          of drift components and wrench dynamics.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-card">
          <h3>Multi-Link Pendulum Models</h3>
          <p>Extended pendulum models with three or more links, providing increasingly complex 
          analogs for understanding the full golfer-club system dynamics.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-card">
          <h3>Pendulum with Flexible Elements</h3>
          <p>Pendulum models incorporating flexible elements, such as a flexible shaft, to model 
          the dynamics of golf clubs with significant shaft deformation.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
